trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Vaishali at Hajipur (Cr.Misc. No.38035 of 2009)
case_name: Sanjeet Kumar Singh @ Sanjeet Kumar v. The State Of Bihar
facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife was suffering from some sort of mental disability or insanity; petitioner sought dissolution of marriage on this ground.

legal_principles.principle: The court cannot act upon a submission without acceptable material, especially when the draft of the Matrimonial Petition brands the lady as a person suffering from psychopathic disorder.
legal_principles.held: It is very difficult to act upon the submission of the petitioner made before the Principal Judge in absence of any acceptable material, specially, when the draft of the Matrimonial Petition brands the lady as a person suffering from psychopathic disorder which, to me, is a very serious mental disorder.

legal_principles.principle: The court cannot accept a serious mental disorder without valid medical check up by some organized institutions or experts.
legal_principles.held: Whether it is a truth or it is simply a ploy to crate a ground for dissolving the marriage is not yet known to the courts inasmuch as there is no order placed before me that indeed the lady suffers from any of the disabilities or mental illness.

outcome.final_order: Court directed the trial court to secure the appearance of the lady and verify the factual correctness of the averment of the petitioner in his Matrimonial Petition.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for dissolution of marriage
advising on mental health issues in family law cases
conducting research on Hindu Marriage Act
